utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Niemann, are you ready to proceed with your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The next witness will be taken by my colleague, Mr. Tieger, but at this stage I might just mention we have served on Mr. Wladimiroff and we will file an up-to-date witness list of the witnesses that we anticipate calling over the next two weeks. The order of witnesses in some cases changed slightly from what was originally intended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Some witnesses have refused to testify so we will not be able to call them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would not encourage that. That is very sad if that occurs, and you know that is just my humour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour. Some of the witnesses are not available at this stage and some other of the witnesses we wish to speak to because they are reluctant to testify, but if we speak to them we may be able to discuss protective measures with them. So that is some of the reasons why the list has been changed slightly from what was originally intended, but that is available now and I can file that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Maybe now is a good time to point out for the record once again Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal that deals with contempt. As you remember, we talked about that Friday. So once again, I wish to make it clear that the Tribunal is very serious and very concerned that witnesses not be intimidated or interfered with in any way. If that comes to the attention of the Trial Chamber, we will enforce without hesitation Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal which provides that, "any person who attempts to interfere with or intimidate a witness may be found guilty of contempt and sentenced in accordance with subrule (A)"; subrule (A) of our Rules provides that, "anyone who is found guilty of contempt can be fined in a sum not exceeding $10,000 or a term of imprisonment not exceeding six months". That is a matter that the Trial Chamber is very concerned about. It does not expect it to happen, but if it comes to the attention that there is any interference or intimidation, then we will enforce that Rule without hesitation. The lawyers should know that and bring it to our attention, Mr. Wladimiroff and Mr. Niemann, and we will act accordingly. Very good. Mr. Niemann, is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honours. Although it has not been formally filed yet, I will hand a copy of this list to your Honours and we will undertake to file it in due course. There are three copies.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Are we going to proceed, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Pursuant to the court's order, we will be in closed session this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now go into closed session to receive the testimony of the next witness. (Hearing in closed session)
